title: Box the expert in: gates, masks, approval and a container
brief: Add every layer of protection around the experts. In the SQL pack you add a tool_call gate that allows one SELECT statement and a tool_result handler that masks email addresses. In the Kubernetes pack you add an approval gate that fails closed when nobody is watching. In the base pack you replace bash with a version whose spawnHook keeps only a short list of environment variables. You write a Dockerfile and a run script that mounts only what the SQL expert needs. When you finish, a DELETE is refused, emails never reach the model, a headless kube_apply is refused, the expert cannot see your API key through bash, and a container run has no access to the rest of your disk.

starter.note: Edit. Add the tool_call gate for sql_query and the tool_result handler that masks emails. Keep the full rows in details.
New. Preview only: kube_apply with the headless-approval gate. It checks ctx.hasUI, then asks with ctx.ui.confirm.
New. Starts with the scrubbed bash: createBashTool with a spawnHook that keeps PATH, HOME, LANG and KUBECONFIG.
New. Based on pi's own example: slim Node image, bash, ca-certificates, git, ripgrep, pi installed with --ignore-scripts, WORKDIR /workspace, ENTRYPOINT pi.
New. docker run with --rm, --read-only, --tmpfs /tmp, a non-root user, -e DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, the agent folder, the pack read-only and data read-only.
New. A sketch of BashOperations whose exec runs docker exec -i k8s-tools sh -c <command>. Error handling can be left out.
Edit. Add handler lookup by event name and a fake ctx with hasUI and ui.confirm.
New. Calls the handlers directly with fake events. No network.

hints: Test the gate with strings that try to slip past it: a leading space, WITH followed by a DELETE, and two statements joined by a semicolon. Only one SELECT or WITH statement may pass.
A gate that throws also stops the call, so it fails closed. A tool_result handler that throws lets the original result through, so test it with odd content such as an image block.
Copy the shape of the result from the event: map content blocks, keep non-text blocks as they are, and mask only the text.
In the approval gate decide on purpose. Check ctx.hasUI first, return block with a clear reason when it is false, and only then call confirm.
For the scrubbed bash, register the tool by spreading the created tool and forwarding execute. Test it by asking the expert to run env: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY must not appear.
A container does not hide environment variables you pass with -e, and the network stays open for the model API. Say that in a comment at the top of the run script.

rubric.criterion: The tool_call gate blocks anything but one SELECT or WITH statement with a reason the model can read, and the database is also open read-only
The tool_result handler replaces email-like strings with [email] in content and keeps the full rows in details
kube_apply is blocked with a clear reason when hasUI is false, blocked when the person declines, and allowed only on yes
A short note in packs/base/SECURITY.md says gates only stop what they were written to stop, and lists what the pi process can still reach
The run script mounts the agent folder, the pack read-only and the data read-only, uses a read-only root and a non-root user, and passes only DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
bash-backend.ts routes commands through docker exec into a k8s-tools container instead of the host shell, and the note names what stays on the host
The scrubbed bash gives a command only PATH, HOME, LANG and KUBECONFIG, and a test shows DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is absent

milestones.title: The SELECT-only gate
milestones.body: Add the tool_call handler to the SQL extension. The test sends DELETE FROM orders, two statements joined by a semicolon, and a plain SELECT. The first two must return block true with the reason Only one SELECT statement is allowed. The last must pass.

milestones.title: Mask results
milestones.body: Add the tool_result handler. A result that holds ada@example.com must reach the model as [email], while details still holds the original rows. A result with a non-text block must pass through unchanged.

milestones.title: Fail closed without a screen
milestones.body: Write the kube_apply approval gate. With hasUI false it must block with a reason. With hasUI true and confirm returning false it blocks. With confirm returning true it returns nothing, which lets the call run.

milestones.title: Scrub the environment
milestones.body: Write the scrubbed bash in the base pack. Set a fake FLEET_SECRET in the test process, run env through the tool, and check that only the four kept names appear in the output.

milestones.title: Run in a container
milestones.body: Build the image and run the SQL expert in it with scripts/run-sql-container.sh, asking it which tables exist. Then ask it to read a file outside the mounts and check that it cannot. This step needs Docker and DEEPSEEK_API_KEY. The test only checks that the script has every flag and that nothing but data is mounted writable.
